title: rossi-model
description: A checked Event-B project: the static-checker model with its formulas as typed trees in Rodin's vocabulary. Version 1. Adding an optional field, an operator name for a new Rodin tag, or a new layer keeps this version, so a consumer must ignore keys it does not know. Renaming or removing a field, or changing what one means, raises it.

name.description: The Rodin project name, which is the leading segment of every handle.

input.description: The input as the caller named it.

prefix.description: The archive prefix this project was found under, when its archive held several.

types.description: Every type the document names, keyed by its canonical Rodin string. Each entry is a whole type, nested inline, so one lookup needs no further resolution.

extensions.description: Every operator extension the document uses.

diagnostics.description: What checking and linting found, in report order. A document is written even when this holds errors; what was rejected is absent from the elements.

id.description: What a span names as its file.

path.description: Where the text came from, when that differs from the id.

type.description: A type as a tree, mirroring Rodin's type objects.

id.description: The extension's identity. Its tag is assigned per process and is never its identity.

span.description: Byte offsets with an exclusive end, plus 1-based lines and character columns. Absent when the component came from Rodin XML, which carries no source text, on an element inherited from another component, whose positions belong to that component's text, and on the nodes a before-after predicate synthesizes.

file.description: The source id. Present on an element; on a node only when it was inherited from another component, whose text its offsets index. A node that leaves it off belongs to the file its element names.

op.description: Rodin's constant name for the operator. Only the names this model can emit are listed: Rodin's three deprecated projection spellings never appear, and neither do rossi's own type-ascription and predicate-application nodes, which cannot reach a checked formula.

node.description: One expression, predicate or bound-identifier declaration. Children follow Rodin's child positions, so a path through them is a path through the formula in Rodin.

tag.description: Rodin's numeric tag. A tag at or above 1000 is an extension's, assigned per process.

type.description: The solved type, as a key into the document's type table. Expressions and declarations have one; predicates never do.

name.description: A free identifier's name, a declaration's name, the name a bound occurrence resolves to, or a predicate variable's name.

index.description: A bound occurrence's de Bruijn index, counting binders outward from 0. Within one declaration list, index 0 is the last declaration. An occurrence with no declaration in scope reports an index and no name.

value.description: An integer literal in decimal. Always a string, because these are unbounded.

form.description: How a comprehension or quantified union was written. Purely syntactic, and not recoverable from the tree. IdentList is rossi's own spelling of a set of identifiers.

assignment.description: An assignment. Rodin gives these no child positions, so instead of a numbered list they name their parts.

idents.description: The assigned variables, always free identifiers.

values.description: BECOMES_EQUAL_TO: the assigned values, one per target.

primed.description: BECOMES_SUCH_THAT: the after-state declarations the predicate binds. A primed occurrence inside pred is a bound identifier resolving to one of these.

pred.description: BECOMES_SUCH_THAT: the relation between the before and after states.

ident.description: A carrier set, constant or event parameter.

inherited_from.description: The machine an inherited parameter was written in.

handle.description: The Rodin handle of the checked element, as its checked file would carry it.

variable.description: A machine variable. There is no owner to record: the checked model keeps the visible set with no note of which ancestor declared each name, so abstract is the inheritance marker, exactly as in Rodin's checked file.

abstract.description: Declared by a machine this one refines.

predicate.description: An axiom, invariant, guard or witness.

label.description: For a witness this is the identifier being witnessed, which for an after-state is a primed name, as in Rodin.

theorem.description: Absent on a witness, which cannot be a theorem.

inherited_from.description: The machine an inherited invariant or guard was written in.

text.description: The predicate as Rodin's checked file spells it, so a consumer can hand it to a Rodin parser and get the same formula back. Type ascriptions appear here wherever Rodin writes them, though the tree has no node for them.

expression.description: Absent when the variant was kept despite naming something unknown, so there is no typed expression to report.

inherited_from.description: The machine an inherited action was written in.

assignment.description: Absent for skip, which has no assignment.

ba.description: The before-after predicate: the same action as a relation between the states, where an after-state value is an ordinary primed identifier. Absent for skip. Its synthesized nodes carry no span.

event.description: An event, carrying the whole chain an extended event inherits.

extended.description: Whether the event extends its abstract counterpart rather than restating it.

accurate.description: Whether checking this event was complete. False means part of it was dropped, and diagnostics says why.

refines.description: The abstract events this one refines. More than one is a merge.

accurate.description: Whether checking this context was complete.

ancestors.description: Every extended context, transitively, oldest first.

accurate.description: Whether checking this machine was complete.

refines.description: The machine this one refines, if any.

ancestors.description: Every refined machine, transitively, oldest first.

internal_contexts.description: Every context visible here, transitively, in the order the checker makes them visible.

invariants.description: Inherited invariants first, oldest machine first, then this machine's own.

events.description: Initialisation first, then the events in source order.

rule_id.description: The rule that produced the finding, where one did.

origin.description: What the finding is about: a component name, optionally followed by a label.
